newsitem.title: RWANDA: Aid workers in Rwanda debate action after killings.
newsitem.headline: Aid workers in Rwanda debate action after killings.

text.p: International aid agencies met in the Rwandan capital on Monday to decide whether to suspend their relief operations in some parts of the country after three Spanish colleagues were shot dead in cold blood by Hutu rebels.

Non-governmental organisations and U.N. agencies met behind closed doors in Kigali. One group has already suspended operations in the small Central African country and Spain has advised its nationals to leave.

Hutu militiamen of the former Rwandan government shot dead three Spanish aid workers and three Rwandan soldiers and seriously wounded an American in an overnight attack in the northwestern town of Ruhengeri on Sunday.

The killers were said by Rwandan military sources to have belonged to the Hutu Interahamwe militia that played a leading role in the 1994 slaughter of 800,000 Rwandans, mostly minority Tutsis, before being driven into Zaire by Tutsi rebels.
Former militiamen are believed to have infiltrated Rwanda among the mass of over 500,000 refugees who returned to their homeland from Zaire late last year.

U.N. spokesman John McMillan told reporters that aid agency operations in Ruhengeri would be limited to the daytime and expatriate workers would not be allowed to spend a night in the city which is close to the border with Zaire.
He said a meeting with government officials later on Monday would discuss security in general and what measures to take following the Ruhengeri killings.

A U.S. diplomat said the attackers stormed into the house and demanded the Spaniards' passports. They were then disturbed by the noise of gunfire outside the house and reacted by shooting the three at close range through the head.
The Spaniards were attached to the Spanish charity Medicos del Mundo (Doctors of the World). It named them as Dr Manuel Madrazo, 42, nurse Maria Flors Sirera, 33, and Luis Valtuena, 30.

The American, Nitin Madhav, 28, from the Pittsburgh area of Pennyslvania, was shot in the leg as he dived behind a table. He was treated in Ruhengeri hospital, where his leg was amputated, and later flown to Kigali and evacuated to Kenya for further treatment.
In Paris, the parent group Medecins du Monde announced that it was suspending all activities in Rwanda pending further information about the killings.
Most expatriates in the Ruhengeri area have left for Kigali.
"The mood is very sombre," a Western diplomat said.
A senior Rwandan military officer told Reuters that the Hutu rebels were seeking to scare away foreigners.

The attack was the latest in a series involving foreign workers in the area near the border with Zaire. U.N. officials warned on Saturday that escalating violence could force the suspension of humanitarian operations in some areas.
Claude Dusaidi, political adviser to Rwandan military strongman and Vice-President Major-General Paul Kagame, told Reuters the government would beef up security following the murders.
"We are going to beef up our security. They (aid agencies) have been refusing our security. They have always preferred to operate on their own," Dusaidi said.
A senior security official, who declined to be named, said Rwanda would also launch a major crackdown on suspected rebels.
